relevance_note: Case report of one patient with a TNFAIP3 variant: "we present a patient with a novel mutation in the TNFAIP3 gene".
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON from hand-entered values (no table transcription). In scope: the index patient ('patient', single unnamed patient of a case report); both parents ('mother of patient', 'father of patient'), described in relation to him and tested negative for the variant; and the two children of the case report cited as (8) ('ref (8) patient' = the 3-year-old, 'ref (8) patient 2' = the 6-month-old), included under the v4 rule because the paper gives their ages and a group statement naming both (normal lymphocyte percentages). No variant rows for the ref (8) children: the text says only 'child with HA20' and prints no variant. The sentence 'the concentration of serum IgG was elevated' does not say which of the two ref (8) children it applies to, so it was not recorded for either. Group-level counts from the first cohort of 16 patients (ref 4) and from Yu et al. (ref 6, 61 patients) were not turned into rows. Tables 1 and 2 (flow cytometry, T-cell differentiation) are patient-level lab values with no ' / ' stacked cells; only the DNT percentages were used as detail. Onset: the Case presentation says 'Fevers started at 7 weeks of age' while the Discussion says symptoms 'since early infancy, from the age of 2 years old'; onset recorded as 7 weeks from the case narrative, and this inconsistency is noted here. In silico predictions (CADD, MutationTaster) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Variant type 'nonsense' is from the authors' statement that the substitution changes glutamine into a termination codon ('resulted in a stop codon'). Checklist choices: 'no arthritis' and 'never noticed rashes' are narrower than the composite items 'arthritis or arthralgia' and 'skin lesions (...)', so those stay 'not reported'; ANA negative (and normal celiac serology) does not exclude the composite 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)', left 'not reported'; 'pronounced lymphatic hypertrophy in the terminal ileum' was not counted as lymphoproliferation/lymphadenopathy (left 'not reported'); 'growth failure' excluded from the statements that growth was normal, although intrauterine growth retardation is recorded as a separate prenatal feature. Normal investigations recorded per D-27: endoscopy 'the investigation was normal' apart from lymphatic hypertrophy was not converted into specific exclusions; 'Infections were excluded' (endoscopy context) was not recorded as a feature. Both the case narrative and the Discussion state the absence of rash and arthritis, so each is recorded twice with its own span (consistent, not contradictory). No contradictions between features were found.
